Processing Notes: Vegetation cover (carbon proxy) in disturbed vs. control plots. Monitoring of a marsh stopped once its disturbed plots had recovered, so after 2014 only the slowest sites remain; the balanced panel of all 12 sites (2010-2014) was analyzed.
Data Citation: Pennings, S. C. (2022). Data from: “Critical slowing down: vegetation height, cover and composition assess resilience of tidal fresh, brackish and salt marshes following experimental disturbance at twelve sites across the estuarine landscape ver 13.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/6df40a30859a7293db9a76fc4fff8cec

Response Variable: Marsh grass shoot mass (g per shoot; biomass proxy)
Processing Notes: TIDE marsh grass shoot mass (biomass proxy): mean shoot mass per species summed across species per transect; species, creek and branch codes were trimmed of stray whitespace. Reference creeks are West and Nelson; Sweeney (2004-2012) and Clubhead (2005, 2009-2019) were treated as nutrient-enriched only in the years they were fertilized, and other creek-years were dropped.
Data Citation: Deegan, L., Warren, S. & Mozdzer, T. (2022). Data from: “Marsh plant species shoot height, weight and diameters for Rowley River tidal creeks associated with long term fertilization experiments, Rowley and Ipswich, MA. ver 5.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/226fb7db2c7b9f8119e40c937b1a19a0

Manipulation: Vegetation removal (annual and continual kelp removal)
Response Variable: Reef algae and invertebrate dry biomass (g m-2)
Processing Notes: Long-term kelp-removal experiment; annual and continual removal vs. control transects. The missing-value code -99999 was set to missing. Response = summed dry biomass of understory algae and invertebrates (mobile fish and the removed giant kelp excluded). January 2008 surveys, which preceded the first removal, were excluded. Treatments were compared with the control transect at the same reef.
Data Citation: Reed, D. C. & Miller, R. J. (2024). Data from: “SBC LTER: Reef: Long-term experiment: biomass of kelp forest species, ongoing since 2008 ver 13.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/4c63cd36279b7e8448d09651a51ed8a6

Experiment: Upper Phillips Creek inundation and wrack experiment
Processing Notes: Upper Phillips Creek inundation and wrack experiment: wrack was laid over half of each of nine plots in April 1994. The wrack half (transect W) was compared with the no-wrack half (V) of the same plots, 1994-1998; response = live aboveground biomass (species summed per 0.0625 m2 quadrat, x16 to g m-2, quadrats averaged per plot). The package does not identify which plots were flooded, so the inundation treatment was not analyzed.
Data Citation: Christian, R. (2019). Data from: “End of Year Biomass for the 1st UPC Inundation Experiment in Upper Phillips Creek marsh 1999-2014 ver 24.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/3854929ce06dc8c667eff9615adb730f

Experiment: TV010 experimental watersheds (WS06 clearcut, WS07 shelterwood, WS08 control)
Response Variable: Mean tree diameter at breast height (cm; biomass proxy)
Processing Notes: Tree remeasurement table (TV010 entity 2). Watersheds WS06 (clearcut) and WS07 (shelterwood) vs. control WS08; all live stems (status 1-3) with a measured DBH; mean DBH per plot and census. The control was censused one year after the treatments (2003/2009/2015 vs. 2002/2008/2014); control census years were aligned to the treatment census periods.
Data Citation: Franklin, J. F., Bell, D. M., Remillard, S. M., Pabst, R. J., Bluhm, A. & Powers, M. (2025). Data from: “Long-term growth, mortality and regeneration of trees in permanent vegetation plots in the Pacific Northwest, 1910 to present ver 28.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/dc4be3db15934e0e5eb4820f56e5d569

Experiment: MELNHE (Multiple Element Limitation in Northern Hardwood Ecosystems)
Processing Notes: MELNHE fall litterfall mass per stand; control vs. N, P, NP and Ca. Fertilization began in spring 2011, so 2009-2010 (pre-treatment) were excluded. Treatments were compared with the control plot of the same stand.
Data Citation: Yanai, R. D., Fisk, M. C., Vadeboncoeur, M. A., Zukswert, J. M., Mann, T., Young, A., Walsh, G., Morley, M. & See, C. R. (2024). Data from: “Multiple Element Limitation in Northern Hardwood Ecosystems (MELNHE): Litterfall mass 2009-2022 ver 1.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/e2d437bddf1166a733b0df09c87f89f1

Processing Notes: Prospect Hill soil respiration (hf005-05). The heated treatment was compared with the disturbance control (cables installed but not heated), which spans the full record; the undisturbed control (1991-2002) was not used. The two June 1991 dates preceding the start of heating were excluded; fluxes were averaged per plot and year.
Data Citation: Frey, S. & Melillo, J. (2024). Data from: “Prospect Hill Soil Warming Experiment at Harvard Forest since 1991 ver 37.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/abf59a218a5868baf5b2c073a7dd1d7f

Processing Notes: Canopy Trimming Experiment soil CO2 flux; block x plot treatment map from the package metadata. The canopy was trimmed between October 2004 and April 2005, so 2003-2004 and the 2005 dates preceding each block's trimming were excluded; chambers were averaged per plot and date.
Data Citation: Silver, W. (2023). Data from: “Canopy Trimming Experiment (CTE) trace gases ver 678951.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/97823bf81da5abf22f8f9d8f3778fc58

Processing Notes: Cascade whole-lake N + P additions: Peter Lake (2013-2015, 2019) and Tuesday Lake (2013-2015) vs. the unmanipulated reference, Paul Lake, in the same years; response = mean manual chlorophyll (carbon proxy) over the sampling season. Lake-years without additions were not paired.
Data Citation: Buelo, C. D., Pace, M. L., Carpenter, S. R., Stanley, E. H., Ortiz, D. A. & Ha, D. T. (2022). Data from: “Cascade Project at North Temperate Lakes LTER – Daily Bloom Data for Whole Lake Experiments 2011 - 2019 ver 2.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/5a9862187368b616bed8e20381343717

Manipulation: CO2 enrichment; N fertilization; species richness
Processing Notes: BioCON aboveground biomass, August (peak) harvest only (a June harvest exists only for 1998-2011). The missing-value code 9999 was set to missing; litter and bare-ground records were excluded; plot totals were averaged per ring x treatment. BioCON contains nested designs on different plot sets (main CO2 x N experiment, 4-species 'S' plots, water manipulation from 2007, water x warming from 2012 in the 9-species plots); each treatment was compared with the ambient control of its own design, and those ambient controls were not counted as treatments. Four plots that lost one factor label from 2013 were restored (2) or dropped (2).
Data Citation: Reich, P. (2024). Data from: “Plant aboveground biomass data: BioCON : Biodiversity, Elevated CO2, and N Enrichment ver 13.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/c153c4eb2414bb1ec2ab8b07adc17ef2

Response Variable: Total herbaceous aboveground biomass (crop + weeds + cover crops; g m-2)
Processing Notes: Compiled herbaceous-biomass table (crop, weeds and cover crops) for the annual cropping systems T1, T2, T3 and T21, with T4 (biologically based, no chemical inputs) as the reference; whole-plant (WHOLE) records were used where reported, so that fractions were not double-counted; litter excluded; stations averaged within replicate and campaigns summed within year. The record begins in 1993, when all systems began to follow one crop sequence; the perennial alfalfa system (T6) was not analyzed.
Data Citation: Robertson, G. & Snapp, S. (2020). Data from: “Annual Net Primary Production on the Main Cropping System Experiment at the Kellogg Biological Station, Hickory Corners, MI (1990 to 2018) ver 85.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/f9b2a038b8a7ad43a252587a84935f30

Manipulation: Fire; mowing; N and P fertilization
Processing Notes: Belowground Plot Experiment (burn x mow x nutrient) vs. the unburned, unmowed, unfertilized plots. Response = herbaceous production per 0.1 m2 quadrat (live grass + forbs + current-year dead, which was sorted separately until 2002; woody stems excluded). Quadrats were averaged per plot and date; the two within-year clips of mowed plots were summed, and the last (peak) clip was used for unmowed plots. Treatments were analyzed only while applied: mowing through 2003 and fertilization through 2016.
Data Citation: Blair, J. & Zeglin, L. (2023). Data from: “PBB01 Belowground Plot Experiment: Aboveground net primary productivity of tallgrass prairie based on accumulated plant biomass ver 15.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/d769700c0e40751bfb8b4fb8c34dabb2

Processing Notes: N fertilization experiment; biomass summed over species within quadrat, quadrats averaged per plot and season; fertilized vs. control plots.
Data Citation: Baur, L., Collins, S., Muldavin, E., Rudgers, J. A. & Pockman, W. T. (2024). Data from: “Nitrogen Fertilization Experiment (NFert): Seasonal Biomass and Seasonal and Annual NPP Data at the Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge, New Mexico ver 208431.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/9468c8bcda68c0a05c06499ec51b1d55

Experiment: Toolik Lake moist acidic tussock tundra experiment
Processing Notes: Late-July (peak-season) harvest of each year; aboveground vascular tissues only ('new above' and 'old above'; mosses and lichens were sorted only from 1989, and belowground tissues and litter are excluded); per-quadrat masses of every harvested quadrat scaled to g m-2 (x25) and averaged per block. The 2015 harvest was recovered from the raw quadrat masses. Greenhouse and shade treatments have only two harvests and were not classified.
Data Citation: Shaver, G. (2017). Data from: “Above ground plant biomass in a mesic acidic tussock tundra experimental site from 1982 to 2015 Arctic LTER, Toolik Lake, Alaska. ver 8.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/c3ef07e6ed81c1fc33e9bc20aff07093

Experiment: CiPEHR (Carbon in Permafrost Experimental Heating Research)
Processing Notes: Half-hourly growing-season NEE from five period files (2009-2021). The 2012 treatment codes (WW/SW) were recoded to those used in other years (W/S). NEE was summed over the season per plot and averaged across the plots of each fence x treatment. Control = ambient winter and summer (C C).
Data Citation: Rodenhizer, H. G., Mauritz, M., Taylor, M., Ledman, J., Natali, S. & Schuur, E. (2022). Data from: “Eight Mile Lake Research Watershed, Carbon in Permafrost Experimental Heating Research (CiPEHR): Half-hourly growing season, chamber-based, CO2 flux data, 2009-2021 ver 23.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/5ee6a71835606934afda8e3eb9a38763

Processing Notes: Soil CO2 flux after amendment (POST_CO2); water-only (W) plots are the control and C, N, P, CN and CP the treatments (unamended plots were not used). Block numbers are reused in the two lake basins, so a replicate is a basin x block, and treatments were compared with the control of the same basin.
Data Citation: Virginia, R. & Wall, D. (2016). Data from: “McMurdo Dry Valleys Stoichiometry Experiment - CO2 ver 5.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/f2c3854f11c24c54be3f3828c130746f

Experiment: Snow x N x temperature experiment (Niwot Saddle)
Manipulation: Fertilization (N; ambient snow and temperature plots)
Processing Notes: Snow x N x temperature factorial; only ambient-snow, ambient-temperature plots were retained so that the N contrast has an uncontaminated control. Live biomass only (litter is reported separately from 2007; the 2006 harvest did not separate them, so the record begins in 2007).
Data Citation: Suding, K. N., Smith, J. G. & Ashton, I. W. (2024). Data from: “Increased temperature, N and snowpack experiment for north of saddle, 2006 - ongoing. ver 7.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/caacfd0b6e32b5a72f8fe3904ca897bf

Response Variable: Annual herbaceous plant biomass (g per 0.25 m2)
Processing Notes: Spring annual-plant biomass per 0.25 m2 quadrat, averaged from sub-plot to plot within site; control plot C1 vs. N, P and N+P. 2018 was excluded because 141 of 144 quadrats contained no annual plants.
Data Citation: Grimm, N., Hall, S. J., Kaye, J. & Allen, J. (2024). Data from: “Desert Fertilization Experiment: investigation of Sonoran desert ecosystem response to atmospheric deposition and experimental nutrient addition, ongoing since 2006 ver 17.” Environmental Data Initiative. Available at: https://doi.org/10.6073/pasta/fd7e336a9493e780777d97bb08ff2352
